_note: Camera roles were established by visually inspecting one daylight frame from each camera on 2026-08-26. LTA burns direction labels into the images; the analysis prompt relies on those labels rather than on hardcoded carriageway geometry. Night behaviour is NOT verified - the model reports image_quality per run and the client falls back to patterns when confidence is low.

2702.shows: The ramp carrying Singapore traffic up onto the Causeway, plus the BKE carriageway leaving the checkpoint. This is the single best outbound queue signal at Woodlands.

2701.shows: The Causeway deck itself, both carriageways, looking across the strait. Shows whether vehicles are moving on the crossing or standing still.

2704.shows: The BKE roughly 2 km south of the checkpoint. Normally free-flowing even when the checkpoint is busy - traffic here means the queue has spilled back onto the expressway, which is a severe signal.

4713.shows: The ramp splitting towards Johor and back towards the AYE at Tuas Checkpoint. Best outbound queue signal at Tuas.

4703.shows: The Second Link bridge deck, both carriageways. Heavy goods traffic is normal here; judge spacing and movement, not vehicle type.

4712.shows: The AYE roughly 800 m before Tuas Checkpoint. Normally free-flowing - queuing here means the checkpoint queue has reached the expressway.
